title: Failed It! How to Turn Mistakes into Ideas and Other Advice for Successfully Screwing Up

description.main: A small paperback in which Erik Kessels argues that mistakes and imperfection drive creative work. It gathers over 150 visual examples from art, design, photography, architecture and product design, with tips and quotations on failing well.
description.extended:
Erik Kessels's Failed It! is a pocket-sized argument for error as a working method in art and design.

Kessels contends that people have become afraid of failure and that the digital undo command lets work stay too perfect to turn into anything else. The book answers with more than 150 visual examples drawn from art, design, photography, architecture and product design, set beside short pieces of advice, quotations and anecdotes. It is part photobook and part guide, published by Phaidon as a 168-page paperback.

Kessels is the co-founder and creative director of the Amsterdam communications agency KesselsKramer. As an artist and collector he has published several books of found photographs and started the magazine Useful Photography. He received the Amsterdam Prize for the Arts in 2010.

notes: Phaidon lists a 168-page paperback; some retailers give 165 pages and an April 2016 date. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
